chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Aban, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyam, from Amr ibn Aqim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For every forty houses, they are neighbors, from in front of him, and from behind him, and from his right, and from his left.'
ai.seo_question: How many houses constitute a neighborhood in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential boundary of neighborhood as a radius of forty houses, a metric widely cited by Shia jurists for determining the extent of neighborly rights (huquq al-jiran). It underscores the communal nature of Islamic social ethics, where proximity creates binding obligations of care and respect among residents.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, from Amro bin Ikrama, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every forty houses (its inhabitants) are neighbours, from in front of him, and from behind him, and from his right, and from his left’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from ‘Amr ibn ‘Akramah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Every forty houses from the front, back, right and left are neighbors. ’”
